newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minister works on despite scandal.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister works on despite scandal.

text.p: Justice Minister Valentin Kovalyov, accused of frolicking with naked women in a gangland sauna, was working at his office on Monday in spite of Sunday's announcement that he was being suspended from his post.
"We have not received any instructions and the minister spent all day working as usual," a ministry spokesman said.
The weekly newspaper Sovershenno Sekretno (Top Secret) last week published grainy snaps taken from a video which it said showed Kovalyov in a sauna with women in September 1995.
Kovalyov, 53, who is a member of the Kremlin's top-level Security Council, asked Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Saturday to take him off the job until he could clear his name.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Sunday he would be temporarily removed from his post.

Such sex and sleaze scandals are all but unknown in Russia and Justice Ministry sources told Interfax news agency on Monday that Kovalyov, who resigned from the post-Soviet Russian Communist party on his appointment as a minister in January 1995, was planning to sue the racy, widely sold newspaper.

"The minister believes that the publication violated his right to privacy," Interfax quoted the source as saying. "If we allow hidden cameras to pursue us everywhere we will have to say goodbye to hopes of building a law-based society in this country."

The ministry spokesman said he knew nothing of Kovalyov's plans. Chernomyrdin has the authority to suspend ministers but the request was addressed to Yeltsin. Only the president can sack ministers outright.
Yeltsin arrived home on Monday from a world leaders' meeting in the United States. A presidential spokesman said he had no information whether Yeltsin approved of suspending Kovalyov.
